description: Knowledge Kit dream flow (issue #671): distil accumulated Claude Code and Codex sessions into proposed memory claims and re-render budgeted briefs. Callable by a host scheduler; never schedules itself and is disabled until the operator enables it. ingest (runtime-session residue, cursor read) -> distil (memory claims through a Relay model runtime) -> route (routed-review policy) -> propose (Corpus create proposals; the run cannot apply one) -> brief (global and per-project, hard byte budgets) -> report (per-run, reconciled with the store) -> cursor (committed last). Executable logic: dream/run.js.

expects.description: Runtime-session residue was read from the committed cursor inside host-authorised transcript roots. Ingest writes nothing and returns a candidate cursor. A rotated or unreadable telemetry file blocks the run and holds the cursor.

Each complete sitting was distilled into memory claims by a model call routed through a Relay runtime (Datum role, Dispatch routing). A sitting whose every extraction pass failed fails the run; it is not read as a sitting with nothing in it.
Every claim has a recomputable routing decision. A claim no rule flags is recorded as proposed; a flagged claim is routed to Survey review. Routing never blocks recall and never promotes a claim.
Claims were staged with Corpus proposeCreate and reconciled by claim id, so a replay creates no duplicate. The run applies nothing: only a reviewer other than the proposer promotes a proposal.

The global brief and each project brief are at or under their byte budgets, ranked by confidence x recency x scope-match, and contain only reviewed claims unless the operator opted in to labelled unreviewed ones.
The per-run report exists and its created and reused counts equal the receipts it lists and the proposals the store gained.
The cursor was committed after every other step succeeded, and not at all when any step failed. It never passes an incomplete sitting, one over the per-run cap, or one that failed.
